pages.text: $(bold)Bountiful$() boards post jobs: bring brass, kill pillagers. A new board pays in kit (iron tools, chainmail, winter fur); a grown one in emerald blocks, saddles and enchanted books.$(br2)Each finished bounty raises the board's standing, shared by all. At ten, $(bold)sealed rumours$() (a map to a boss); at fifteen, journals and totems; at thirty, a named weapon.
The capital's board works for everyone; a new town can craft its own. Decrees set what a board asks for; Archivist's Records pays in writings.

$(bold)Caravans & Convoys$(): merchant caravans travel between settlements with wagons, and you can run your own. Build a stop and routes open. This is the mid-game economy before rail.$(br2)Raiders know the roads too.

Late game, the $(bold)Trading Floor$() lets a train sell on a schedule: a depot in a real town, goods in, emeralds out, while you are elsewhere.$(br2)Depots need a Blueprint and a town with a bell and beds. There is no version that works in a hole in the ground.
